security_audit.summary: All static findings were reviewed against the Markdown source. The alerts are false positives from documentation links, inline command formatting, lark-cli examples, and Lark event schema references. No prompt injection, malicious intent, or data exfiltration instruction was found.

remediation.issue: Relative Markdown links use parent-directory paths that trigger traversal scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Replace parent-directory links with marketplace-safe references or include shared prerequisites inside the packaged skill.

remediation.issue: Command examples use Markdown backticks and shell fences that static tools may misread as executable code.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note that examples are documentation and should run only after confirming Lark identity, scope, and user intent.

remediation.issue: Authorized event streams can contain sensitive workspace content and identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy note recommending least-privilege scopes, bounded sampling, and careful handling of saved event output.

content.user_title: Consume Lark Events in Real Time
content.value_statement: Lark event streams are difficult to monitor consistently across messages, tasks, meetings, minutes, and whiteboards. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through lark-cli commands, schemas, filters, and bounded consumers.
actual_capabilities: Lists available Lark EventKeys and explains their product areas.
Shows how to inspect event schemas before writing filters.
Guides bounded event consumption with max event and timeout controls.
Explains jq filters for messages, tasks, meetings, minutes, and whiteboards.
Documents subscription lifecycle behavior for events with pre-consume hooks.
Describes multi-process consumption when monitoring several EventKeys.
limitations: Requires lark-cli, valid Lark authentication, and the needed product scopes.
Does not create or host a webhook server.
Cannot bypass Lark permission checks or missing app scopes.
Long-running consumers need external process supervision and cleanup.

use_cases.title: Monitor Bot Messages
use_cases.description: Build a consumer that streams bot message events and filters by chat type, message type, or sender.

use_cases.title: Track Workspace Task Changes
use_cases.description: Consume task update events and project compact records for audit, notification, or workflow systems.

use_cases.title: React to Meeting and Whiteboard Activity
use_cases.description: Subscribe to meeting, minutes, note, or whiteboard events and handle their lifecycle safely.

prompt_templates.title: List Available Events
prompt_templates.prompt: List the Lark EventKeys I can consume. Group them by product area and tell me which identity each key needs.

prompt_templates.title: Sample One Message Event
prompt_templates.prompt: Consume one sample IM receive event with a timeout. Explain the important fields and whether content is plain text or card JSON.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Filtered Consumer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a jq filter that streams only group text messages from one chat and returns sender, message ID, and content.

prompt_templates.title: Operate Multiple Subscribers
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a bounded monitoring workflow for IM, task, and whiteboard events. Include lifecycle handling, cleanup, and failure responses.

output_examples.input: Monitor new Lark messages for one bot.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the IM receive event, recommends bot identity, explains content handling, and suggests a bounded sample before continuous monitoring.

output_examples.input: Track task changes visible to a user.
output_examples.output: The skill explains the task update event, required scope, subscription behavior, and the fields useful for downstream notifications.
The skill describes the required whiteboard token, manage access requirement, subscription lifecycle, and editor identifier fields.

best_practices: Use max event or timeout bounds for sampling before starting continuous consumers.
Read schema output before writing jq filters because field roots and decoded state vary.
Use the least privileged Lark identity and scopes that satisfy the event stream.
anti_patterns: Starting unbounded consumers without process supervision or a cleanup plan.
Assuming every event has the same root path or raw payload shape.
Using quiet mode in automated runs because it hides readiness and diagnostics.

faq.question: Does this skill create a webhook server?
faq.answer: No. It documents lark-cli event consumption through local commands and streamed output.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require lark-cli?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill depends on lark-cli and valid Lark or Feishu authentication.

faq.question: Can it listen to multiple EventKeys?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses one consumer process per EventKey, with shared local bus support.

faq.question: Can events be filtered?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains jq filters and recommends checking schemas before filtering.

faq.question: What sensitive data may appear?
faq.answer: Authorized streams can include messages, user identifiers, task data, meeting metadata, minutes, and whiteboard activity.
